items.title: Argus: A General-Purpose Agentic Runtime for Long-Horizon Reasoning
items.abstract: Argus provides a general-purpose agentic runtime for long-horizon reasoning by employing a persistent, self-evolving architecture. It separates user intent from operational details and uses a review process for all new components, allowing agents to persist when successful and pivot when facing issues. This approach significantly improves performance on complex tasks like software engineering benchmarks compared to simpler methods.
items.figure_caption: Argus runtime and breadth evidence. The central diagram shows Manager authority over tasks, research verticals, and Stage transitions; Planner, Engineer, and Reviewer operate over a shared workspace whose knowledge, event log, artifacts, backlog, budget, daemon, and memory persist across bounded missions. The surrounding cards report outcomes from seven task-native evaluations. Their bars use independent scales and indicate comparison direction with arrows; they are breadth evidence rather than a single normalized leaderboard.

items.title: Hierarchical Graph Memory for LLM Agents with Path-level Localization and Rewrite
items.abstract: This paper introduces HiGram, a hierarchical graph memory for LLM agents designed for long-term reasoning. Its core method organizes memories into a coarse-to-fine structure, reducing irrelevant information and improving retrieval efficiency. HiGram's key contribution is this hierarchical organization and a novel path-level rewriting mechanism, enabling more effective and efficient memory updates compared to flat graph approaches.
items.figure_caption: An overview of HiGram . Our method organizes memory into a hierarchical graph structure with upper-level nodes connecting MemoryUnits that store factual information. Then, given a query and an update, our MicroGraph-based path-level localization module retrieves relevant memory MicroGraphs to build a support subgraph, and identifies the affected evidence path. Lastly, coordinated rewriting updates MemoryUnit states and dependency structures within the localized evidence path to maintain consistent memory updates.

items.title: OctoLong: Mid-Training On Cross-Repository Code Contexts Enhances Long-Context Modeling
items.abstract: This paper introduces OctoLong, a method for creating large, dependency-rich code contexts by recursively retrieving code references. They then use these contexts to mid-train open-source language models, resulting in OctoLong-Instruct, which demonstrates enhanced long-context modeling capabilities. The core contribution is a novel approach to generating and utilizing extensive code contexts for improved long-context language model performance.

items.title: When Does Latent Communication Pay? A Causal Audit of Relayed KV Caches in Multi-Agent LLMs
items.abstract: This paper causally audits the claimed benefits of relaying key-value caches (instead of text) in multi-agent LLMs. The core method involves replacing the relayed cache with manipulated versions (deranged, zeroed, random) to isolate the cache's true impact. The contribution is demonstrating that relayed caches only provide significant benefits when the receiver *needs* the sender's private information; otherwise, the gains are negligible and likely artifacts.
items.figure_caption: Causal audit design. The primary contrast holds the receiver and the batch of caches fixed, permuting only which cache reaches each query. Both arms relay an equally well-formed cache, so the true-minus-deranged difference isolates example pairing from any generic benefit of relaying one.

items.title: State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents
items.abstract: State2State is a novel mid-training method for LLM agents that addresses the limitations of supervised fine-tuning and traditional RL. Its core method involves converting explored environment states into training objectives, challenging agents to reach specific target states. This approach enables scalable and verifiable agent training by deriving tasks directly from environment interaction, eliminating the need for expert supervision or manual task design.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of supervision sources for LLM agent training. SFT relies on expert trajectories, and task-centric RL relies on human-specified tasks with task-specific verifiers. In contrast, the environment-only setting studied in this work derives learning signals purely from environment itself.

items.title: Skill-Use: Can LLMs Actually Use Skills in Agentic Harnesses?
items.abstract: This paper introduces Skill-Use, a benchmark to evaluate if LLM agents can effectively recognize and apply skills. The core method involves progressive disclosure, where agents must first retrieve a skill's full procedure based on its name and description before executing it. Skill-Use measures Trigger, Compliance, and Boundary adherence, providing a comprehensive score for an agent's ability to utilize skills autonomously.
items.figure_caption: Composition and coverage of Skill-Use . (a) Domain distribution of the 79 79 skills across nine categories, where the inner ring gives each category’s share and the outer ring lists representative skills. (b) Skill and task counts per domain, where each bubble marks one domain and reports its skill and task totals. (c) Composition of the rubric items by type. (d) Distribution of skill-exclusive requirements per task, our proxy for difficulty, where the dashed line marks the mean.

items.title: A-SR: Self-Evolving Agentic LLMs for Symbolic Regression via Hierarchical Coordination
items.abstract: A-SR introduces a novel self-evolving agentic framework for symbolic regression that moves beyond single-prompt approaches. Its core method involves coordinating specialized LLM agents through role-conditioned evidence views and hierarchical coordination protocols, enabling more effective exploration of the search space. The key contribution is a dynamic, adaptive system that learns from evaluator feedback to refine its search process within a run and distills successful strategies into proposal priors for future runs.
items.figure_caption: Agentic feedback-driven coordination in A-SR. A-SR converts validity, improvement, failure, and complexity signals into coordination decisions over protocol, role, and routed memory, forming the context for the next equation.

items.title: ABSeeker: Training Long-Horizon Search Agents via Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment
items.abstract: ABSeeker trains long-horizon search agents by assigning credit at a finer, step-level rather than trajectory-level. Its core method, Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment (ABC), recovers intermediate clues from the ground-truth answer to generate dense supervision. This allows the agent to learn which actions are truly useful, even in failed trajectories, by rewarding correct steps and penalizing errors or redundancy.
items.figure_caption: ABSeeker achieves the best performance among 4B models and remains competitive with several larger search agents. Striped regions indicate results with context management enabled.

items.title: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Observation-Calibrated Self-Distillation
items.abstract: This paper introduces Observation-Calibrated Self-Distillation (OCSD) to improve reinforcement learning for large language model agents. OCSD addresses a limitation of prior methods by disentangling the influence of privileged information from the replay process itself. It achieves this by contrasting two replay views, one with full information and one with crucial future observations removed, to isolate the true value of the privileged data.
items.figure_caption: Deriving the observation residual from structurally matched replay views.

items.title: ArtAnno: Annotating Implicit Semantics in Artworks through LLM Agent-Driven Bidirectional Human-AI Augmentation
items.abstract: ArtAnno introduces Bidirectional Human-AI Augmentation (BiHAA), a closed-loop framework for annotating implicit artwork semantics. It leverages a multi-agent LLM system where AI proactively suggests semantic labels and humans refine them, creating a continuous feedback loop that enhances both AI capabilities and human annotation efficiency. This approach addresses the limitations of one-way AI assistance in capturing complex, culturally-grounded meanings in art.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Comparison between the Bidirectional Human-AI Augmentation Framework (BiHAA) and traditional frameworks. (A-B) Left block represents input, right one represents output. (C) Both blocks serve as input and output.

items.title: Chained Recursive Language Models for Multi-Iteration Reasoning
items.abstract: This paper introduces Chained Recursive Language Models (Chained RLM), an inference-time architecture that breaks down complex reasoning tasks into smaller, manageable steps. Instead of a single, long inference, Chained RLM repeatedly calls the same model with the original problem and context, but provides each new "reasoning root" with a concise summary and a shared "blackboard" of intermediate results. This approach aims to mitigate error propagation and improve performance on multi-step reasoning tasks by allowing the model to focus on distinct sub-problems at each stage.
items.figure_caption: Chained RLM architecture with 3 RLM calls.

items.title: Gradient Immunity: Null-Space Resistance to Malicious Fine-Tuning
items.abstract: This paper introduces "Gradient Immunity" to defend against malicious fine-tuning of open-weight language models. Their core method, the Unidirectional Safety Gate (USG), uses a novel cubic layer to block harmful gradients and an inverse adapter to preserve normal model behavior. This approach protects safety-critical components in a partially protected open-weight release setting, a scenario not addressed by prior defenses.
items.figure_caption: The figure illustrates the idealized behavior of a USG-style safeguard. For harmful data, it functions as a diode: during backpropagation, the USG sets gradients to zero, inducing gradient vanishing and thereby blocking gradient propagation. For safe data, it acts as a wire without inducing gradient vanishing in the idealized exact-blocking definition. Its core idea is the controllable induction of gradient vanishing—normally an undesirable behavior in model training.

items.title: InsightEmb: Learning Action-Intent Embeddings for Agentic Insight Retrieval
items.abstract: This paper introduces InsightEmb, a novel method for agentic insight retrieval. Unlike previous approaches focusing on semantic similarity, InsightEmb learns embeddings that capture the "progress-oriented" nature of insights, meaning it retrieves insights that help an agent overcome its current decision-making challenges. Its core contribution is a contrastive learning framework that aligns concrete situations with abstract rules and clusters reasoning trajectories based on their progress, enabling effective insight retrieval without environment-specific training.
items.figure_caption: InsightEmb retrieves insights that resolve the agent’s current procedural bottleneck rather than topical overlap alone. Left: the abstraction gap and shared situation-to-insight structure across math and embodied tasks. Right: on an ALFWorld “hot potato” task, Base favors heating rules before the object is found, whereas InsightEmb retrieves search-first guidance.

items.title: OPD-V: Visual On-Policy Self-Distillation with Modality Balance
items.abstract: This paper introduces OPD-V, a novel visual on-policy self-distillation method for multimodal large language models (MLLMs). It addresses the issue of modality imbalance, where text often dominates, hindering full multimodal integration. OPD-V leverages the concept of modality balance itself as privileged information, using a "Positive Teacher" (Zoom-In Image) to guide distillation and improve visual reasoning.
items.figure_caption: Modality Balance as privileged information, evaluated on 5K samples drawn from multiple domains. Left: the Modality-Balance Attention Ratio is lowest for the Negative Teacher with the Mask Image, intermediate for the student with the Original Image, and highest for the Positive Teacher with the Zoom-In Image. These matched conditions expose distinct degrees of Modality Imbalance. Right: as the Modality-Balance Logits Margin increases, the gap between the Positive and Negative Teacher attention ratios widens, accompanied by higher student correctness. For each margin interval b b , the blue curve reports Δ ​ ρ b = | b | − 1 ​ ∑ i ∈ b [ ρ ​ ( c + ; y i ) − ρ ​ ( c − ; y i ) ] \( \Delta \)\( \rho_{b} \)=|b|^{-1}\( \sum_{i\in b} \)[\( \rho \)(c^{+};y_{i})-\( \rho \)(c^{-};y_{i})] , where y i y_{i} is the response trajectory for sample i i , and c + c^{+} and c − c^{-} denote the Zoom-In Image and Mask Image conditions, respectively.

items.title: ORACLE: A Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning-Based Analog Circuit Design Optimizer with Large Language Models-Guided Exploration
items.abstract: ORACLE is a novel reinforcement learning framework for analog circuit design that addresses the limitations of single-objective optimization and scalar reward reduction in multi-objective problems. It employs vector-valued learning and preference-aware conditioning, allowing users to specify desired trade-offs with a preference vector. This enables ORACLE to find true Pareto optimal designs and adapt to changing specifications without retraining.

items.title: Protoreasoning in Tiny Transformers
items.abstract: This paper introduces "protoreasoning," a simplified Chain of Thought method applied to tiny transformer models. By using reasoning-friendly tasks on Dyck languages, the authors demonstrate that these small models can learn to generalize better out-of-distribution when employing protoreasoning. This approach allows for detailed analysis of step-by-step reasoning in models much smaller than typical LLMs, offering insights into how such reasoning is learned.

items.title: Scrouting: Cost-Aware Routing of Coding Agents by Scouting the Repository First
items.abstract: This paper introduces SuperScout, a cost-aware routing method for coding agents. It first uses a "searcher" model to explore the software repository, identifying relevant information and verifying claims. This scouted information, along with the task description, then guides a "router" to select the most appropriate "fixer" model, significantly reducing the cost per solved issue while maintaining high performance.

items.title: EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement
items.abstract: EvolveNet introduces a novel method for improving LLM agents by collaboratively evolving their "harness" (the program that manages context, tools, and execution). Instead of a single optimizer processing all experience, EvolveNet distributes harness evolution to local agent deployments. This allows each deployment to adapt the harness to its specific workload, and then these localized adaptations are composed to create a more robust and universally improved harness.
items.figure_caption: Left: conventional harness evolution is sequential. One optimizer consumes incoming batches in order and each harness must be produced before the next can be explored, so a T T -stage search has serial depth T T and follows a single trajectory. Right: EvolveNet broadcasts the shared harness h ( t ) h^{(t)} to K K clients, which evolve it in parallel on the workloads held at each, into specialists h k ( t ) h_{k}^{(t)} . The server aggregates the returned programs rather than the workloads behind them, adopting a mechanism globally when its supporting evidence spans domains and conditioning it on its home domain otherwise, and commits the result as h ( t + 1 ) h^{(t+1)} only if it passes the per-item acceptance test (Sec. 4.4 ). The dashed edge closes the loop: the committed harness is redistributed, so each client’s next round of evolution starts from what the whole collaboration has learned, not from its own previous program.

items.title: Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-aware Rollout Intervention Learning
items.abstract: This paper introduces Recoverability-Aware Intervention Learning (RAIL), a framework that optimizes how reinforcement learning policies learn from rollouts. Instead of uniform rollout allocation, RAIL dynamically selects and intervenes in rollouts based on their predicted learning improvement, treating it as an online contextual-bandit problem. This approach allows for adaptive intervention strategies that evolve with the policy, leading to more efficient and effective learning.
items.figure_caption: Performance-rollout Results Preview on AgentBench. RAIL achieves the highest success rates with comparable or fewer rollouts than uniform GRPO and adaptive intervention baselines on OS task (Left) and DB task(right). More results on further benchmarks and analysis in Section 4 .

items.title: SparseDitto: Customizing GPU Kernels for Different Sparsity Patterns with LLM-Based Agentic System
items.abstract: SparseDitto is an LLM-based system that automatically generates customized GPU kernels for sparse matrix operations. It addresses the performance variability of existing libraries by adapting the matrix representation, execution strategy, and hardware mapping to specific sparsity patterns and target GPUs. This approach aims to achieve optimal performance across diverse workloads, unlike static implementations.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. One 16 × 16 16\( \times \) 16 matrix exposes intrinsic pattern cues and format-induced costs. The matrix contains an irregular dense tile, a high-degree column, an empty row, and uneven row lengths. CSR and CSC traverse compressed rows and columns, respectively. SELL-C with C = 8 C=8 introduces slice-local padding, while 4 × 4 4\( \times \) 4 BSR introduces block fill. The right column shows the resulting work granularity and imbalance for rows, columns, slice slots, and blocks.

By using reasoning-friendly tasks on Dyck languages, the authors demonstrate that these small models can learn to generalize better out-of-distribution when employing protoreasoning. This approach allows for detailed analysis of step-by-step reasoning in models much smaller than typical LLMs, offering insights into how such reasoning is learned.

arxiv.title: Scrouting: Cost-Aware Routing of Coding Agents by Scouting the Repository First
arxiv.abstract: This paper introduces SuperScout, a cost-aware routing method for coding agents. It first uses a "searcher" model to explore the software repository, identifying relevant information and verifying claims. This scouted information, along with the task description, then guides a "router" to select the most appropriate "fixer" model, significantly reducing the cost per solved issue while maintaining high performance.

arxiv.title: EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement
arxiv.abstract: EvolveNet introduces a novel method for improving LLM agents by collaboratively evolving their "harness" (the program that manages context, tools, and execution). Instead of a single optimizer processing all experience, EvolveNet distributes harness evolution to local agent deployments. This allows each deployment to adapt the harness to its specific workload, and then these localized adaptations are composed to create a more robust and universally improved harness.
arxiv.figure_caption: Left: conventional harness evolution is sequential. One optimizer consumes incoming batches in order and each harness must be produced before the next can be explored, so a T T -stage search has serial depth T T and follows a single trajectory. Right: EvolveNet broadcasts the shared harness h ( t ) h^{(t)} to K K clients, which evolve it in parallel on the workloads held at each, into specialists h k ( t ) h_{k}^{(t)} . The server aggregates the returned programs rather than the workloads behind them, adopting a mechanism globally when its supporting evidence spans domains and conditioning it on its home domain otherwise, and commits the result as h ( t + 1 ) h^{(t+1)} only if it passes the per-item acceptance test (Sec. 4.4 ). The dashed edge closes the loop: the committed harness is redistributed, so each client’s next round of evolution starts from what the whole collaboration has learned, not from its own previous program.

arxiv.title: Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-aware Rollout Intervention Learning
arxiv.abstract: This paper introduces Recoverability-Aware Intervention Learning (RAIL), a framework that optimizes how reinforcement learning policies learn from rollouts. Instead of uniform rollout allocation, RAIL dynamically selects and intervenes in rollouts based on their predicted learning improvement, treating it as an online contextual-bandit problem. This approach allows for adaptive intervention strategies that evolve with the policy, leading to more efficient and effective learning.
arxiv.figure_caption: Performance-rollout Results Preview on AgentBench. RAIL achieves the highest success rates with comparable or fewer rollouts than uniform GRPO and adaptive intervention baselines on OS task (Left) and DB task(right). More results on further benchmarks and analysis in Section 4 .

arxiv.title: SparseDitto: Customizing GPU Kernels for Different Sparsity Patterns with LLM-Based Agentic System
arxiv.abstract: SparseDitto is an LLM-based system that automatically generates customized GPU kernels for sparse matrix operations. It addresses the performance variability of existing libraries by adapting the matrix representation, execution strategy, and hardware mapping to specific sparsity patterns and target GPUs. This approach aims to achieve optimal performance across diverse workloads, unlike static implementations.
arxiv.figure_caption: Figure 1. One 16 × 16 16\( \times \) 16 matrix exposes intrinsic pattern cues and format-induced costs. The matrix contains an irregular dense tile, a high-degree column, an empty row, and uneven row lengths. CSR and CSC traverse compressed rows and columns, respectively. SELL-C with C = 8 C=8 introduces slice-local padding, while 4 × 4 4\( \times \) 4 BSR introduces block fill. The right column shows the resulting work granularity and imbalance for rows, columns, slice slots, and blocks.

papers.title: Argus: A General-Purpose Agentic Runtime for Long-Horizon Reasoning
papers.abstract: Argus provides a general-purpose agentic runtime for long-horizon reasoning by employing a persistent, self-evolving architecture. It separates user intent from operational details and uses a review process for all new components, allowing agents to persist when successful and pivot when facing issues. This approach significantly improves performance on complex tasks like software engineering benchmarks compared to simpler methods.
papers.figure_caption: Argus runtime and breadth evidence. The central diagram shows Manager authority over tasks, research verticals, and Stage transitions; Planner, Engineer, and Reviewer operate over a shared workspace whose knowledge, event log, artifacts, backlog, budget, daemon, and memory persist across bounded missions. The surrounding cards report outcomes from seven task-native evaluations. Their bars use independent scales and indicate comparison direction with arrows; they are breadth evidence rather than a single normalized leaderboard.

papers.title: Hierarchical Graph Memory for LLM Agents with Path-level Localization and Rewrite
papers.abstract: This paper introduces HiGram, a hierarchical graph memory for LLM agents designed for long-term reasoning. Its core method organizes memories into a coarse-to-fine structure, reducing irrelevant information and improving retrieval efficiency. HiGram's key contribution is this hierarchical organization and a novel path-level rewriting mechanism, enabling more effective and efficient memory updates compared to flat graph approaches.
papers.figure_caption: An overview of HiGram . Our method organizes memory into a hierarchical graph structure with upper-level nodes connecting MemoryUnits that store factual information. Then, given a query and an update, our MicroGraph-based path-level localization module retrieves relevant memory MicroGraphs to build a support subgraph, and identifies the affected evidence path. Lastly, coordinated rewriting updates MemoryUnit states and dependency structures within the localized evidence path to maintain consistent memory updates.

papers.title: OctoLong: Mid-Training On Cross-Repository Code Contexts Enhances Long-Context Modeling
papers.abstract: This paper introduces OctoLong, a method for creating large, dependency-rich code contexts by recursively retrieving code references. They then use these contexts to mid-train open-source language models, resulting in OctoLong-Instruct, which demonstrates enhanced long-context modeling capabilities. The core contribution is a novel approach to generating and utilizing extensive code contexts for improved long-context language model performance.

papers.title: When Does Latent Communication Pay? A Causal Audit of Relayed KV Caches in Multi-Agent LLMs
papers.abstract: This paper causally audits the claimed benefits of relaying key-value caches (instead of text) in multi-agent LLMs. The core method involves replacing the relayed cache with manipulated versions (deranged, zeroed, random) to isolate the cache's true impact. The contribution is demonstrating that relayed caches only provide significant benefits when the receiver *needs* the sender's private information; otherwise, the gains are negligible and likely artifacts.
papers.figure_caption: Causal audit design. The primary contrast holds the receiver and the batch of caches fixed, permuting only which cache reaches each query. Both arms relay an equally well-formed cache, so the true-minus-deranged difference isolates example pairing from any generic benefit of relaying one.

papers.title: State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: State2State is a novel mid-training method for LLM agents that addresses the limitations of supervised fine-tuning and traditional RL. Its core method involves converting explored environment states into training objectives, challenging agents to reach specific target states. This approach enables scalable and verifiable agent training by deriving tasks directly from environment interaction, eliminating the need for expert supervision or manual task design.
papers.figure_caption: Comparison of supervision sources for LLM agent training. SFT relies on expert trajectories, and task-centric RL relies on human-specified tasks with task-specific verifiers. In contrast, the environment-only setting studied in this work derives learning signals purely from environment itself.

papers.title: Skill-Use: Can LLMs Actually Use Skills in Agentic Harnesses?
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Skill-Use, a benchmark to evaluate if LLM agents can effectively recognize and apply skills. The core method involves progressive disclosure, where agents must first retrieve a skill's full procedure based on its name and description before executing it. Skill-Use measures Trigger, Compliance, and Boundary adherence, providing a comprehensive score for an agent's ability to utilize skills autonomously.
papers.figure_caption: Composition and coverage of Skill-Use . (a) Domain distribution of the 79 79 skills across nine categories, where the inner ring gives each category’s share and the outer ring lists representative skills. (b) Skill and task counts per domain, where each bubble marks one domain and reports its skill and task totals. (c) Composition of the rubric items by type. (d) Distribution of skill-exclusive requirements per task, our proxy for difficulty, where the dashed line marks the mean.

papers.title: A-SR: Self-Evolving Agentic LLMs for Symbolic Regression via Hierarchical Coordination
papers.abstract: A-SR introduces a novel self-evolving agentic framework for symbolic regression that moves beyond single-prompt approaches. Its core method involves coordinating specialized LLM agents through role-conditioned evidence views and hierarchical coordination protocols, enabling more effective exploration of the search space. The key contribution is a dynamic, adaptive system that learns from evaluator feedback to refine its search process within a run and distills successful strategies into proposal priors for future runs.
papers.figure_caption: Agentic feedback-driven coordination in A-SR. A-SR converts validity, improvement, failure, and complexity signals into coordination decisions over protocol, role, and routed memory, forming the context for the next equation.

papers.title: ABSeeker: Training Long-Horizon Search Agents via Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment
papers.abstract: ABSeeker trains long-horizon search agents by assigning credit at a finer, step-level rather than trajectory-level. Its core method, Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment (ABC), recovers intermediate clues from the ground-truth answer to generate dense supervision. This allows the agent to learn which actions are truly useful, even in failed trajectories, by rewarding correct steps and penalizing errors or redundancy.
papers.figure_caption: ABSeeker achieves the best performance among 4B models and remains competitive with several larger search agents. Striped regions indicate results with context management enabled.

papers.title: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Observation-Calibrated Self-Distillation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Observation-Calibrated Self-Distillation (OCSD) to improve reinforcement learning for large language model agents. OCSD addresses a limitation of prior methods by disentangling the influence of privileged information from the replay process itself. It achieves this by contrasting two replay views, one with full information and one with crucial future observations removed, to isolate the true value of the privileged data.
papers.figure_caption: Deriving the observation residual from structurally matched replay views.

papers.title: ArtAnno: Annotating Implicit Semantics in Artworks through LLM Agent-Driven Bidirectional Human-AI Augmentation
papers.abstract: ArtAnno introduces Bidirectional Human-AI Augmentation (BiHAA), a closed-loop framework for annotating implicit artwork semantics. It leverages a multi-agent LLM system where AI proactively suggests semantic labels and humans refine them, creating a continuous feedback loop that enhances both AI capabilities and human annotation efficiency. This approach addresses the limitations of one-way AI assistance in capturing complex, culturally-grounded meanings in art.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Comparison between the Bidirectional Human-AI Augmentation Framework (BiHAA) and traditional frameworks. (A-B) Left block represents input, right one represents output. (C) Both blocks serve as input and output.

papers.title: Chained Recursive Language Models for Multi-Iteration Reasoning
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Chained Recursive Language Models (Chained RLM), an inference-time architecture that breaks down complex reasoning tasks into smaller, manageable steps. Instead of a single, long inference, Chained RLM repeatedly calls the same model with the original problem and context, but provides each new "reasoning root" with a concise summary and a shared "blackboard" of intermediate results. This approach aims to mitigate error propagation and improve performance on multi-step reasoning tasks by allowing the model to focus on distinct sub-problems at each stage.
papers.figure_caption: Chained RLM architecture with 3 RLM calls.

papers.title: Gradient Immunity: Null-Space Resistance to Malicious Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Gradient Immunity" to defend against malicious fine-tuning of open-weight language models. Their core method, the Unidirectional Safety Gate (USG), uses a novel cubic layer to block harmful gradients and an inverse adapter to preserve normal model behavior. This approach protects safety-critical components in a partially protected open-weight release setting, a scenario not addressed by prior defenses.
papers.figure_caption: The figure illustrates the idealized behavior of a USG-style safeguard. For harmful data, it functions as a diode: during backpropagation, the USG sets gradients to zero, inducing gradient vanishing and thereby blocking gradient propagation. For safe data, it acts as a wire without inducing gradient vanishing in the idealized exact-blocking definition. Its core idea is the controllable induction of gradient vanishing—normally an undesirable behavior in model training.

papers.title: InsightEmb: Learning Action-Intent Embeddings for Agentic Insight Retrieval
papers.abstract: This paper introduces InsightEmb, a novel method for agentic insight retrieval. Unlike previous approaches focusing on semantic similarity, InsightEmb learns embeddings that capture the "progress-oriented" nature of insights, meaning it retrieves insights that help an agent overcome its current decision-making challenges. Its core contribution is a contrastive learning framework that aligns concrete situations with abstract rules and clusters reasoning trajectories based on their progress, enabling effective insight retrieval without environment-specific training.
papers.figure_caption: InsightEmb retrieves insights that resolve the agent’s current procedural bottleneck rather than topical overlap alone. Left: the abstraction gap and shared situation-to-insight structure across math and embodied tasks. Right: on an ALFWorld “hot potato” task, Base favors heating rules before the object is found, whereas InsightEmb retrieves search-first guidance.

papers.title: OPD-V: Visual On-Policy Self-Distillation with Modality Balance
papers.abstract: This paper introduces OPD-V, a novel visual on-policy self-distillation method for multimodal large language models (MLLMs). It addresses the issue of modality imbalance, where text often dominates, hindering full multimodal integration. OPD-V leverages the concept of modality balance itself as privileged information, using a "Positive Teacher" (Zoom-In Image) to guide distillation and improve visual reasoning.
papers.figure_caption: Modality Balance as privileged information, evaluated on 5K samples drawn from multiple domains. Left: the Modality-Balance Attention Ratio is lowest for the Negative Teacher with the Mask Image, intermediate for the student with the Original Image, and highest for the Positive Teacher with the Zoom-In Image. These matched conditions expose distinct degrees of Modality Imbalance. Right: as the Modality-Balance Logits Margin increases, the gap between the Positive and Negative Teacher attention ratios widens, accompanied by higher student correctness. For each margin interval b b , the blue curve reports Δ ​ ρ b = | b | − 1 ​ ∑ i ∈ b [ ρ ​ ( c + ; y i ) − ρ ​ ( c − ; y i ) ] \( \Delta \)\( \rho_{b} \)=|b|^{-1}\( \sum_{i\in b} \)[\( \rho \)(c^{+};y_{i})-\( \rho \)(c^{-};y_{i})] , where y i y_{i} is the response trajectory for sample i i , and c + c^{+} and c − c^{-} denote the Zoom-In Image and Mask Image conditions, respectively.

papers.title: ORACLE: A Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning-Based Analog Circuit Design Optimizer with Large Language Models-Guided Exploration
papers.abstract: ORACLE is a novel reinforcement learning framework for analog circuit design that addresses the limitations of single-objective optimization and scalar reward reduction in multi-objective problems. It employs vector-valued learning and preference-aware conditioning, allowing users to specify desired trade-offs with a preference vector. This enables ORACLE to find true Pareto optimal designs and adapt to changing specifications without retraining.

hacker_news.summary: Hobby programming communities resist LLM usage due to concerns about skill degradation, loss of creative exploration, and the potential for LLMs to undermine the intrinsic value of programming as a craft.
